name: Omri
charge: Doing worse than all that were before him; walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin
summary: After Zimri burned the palace over himself, Israel divided: half followed Tibni and half followed Omri. Omri prevailed, reigned twelve years, bought the hill Samaria, and built the city that became the northern kingdom’s capital. He wrought evil in the eyes of the Lord and did worse than all that were before him.
offense: After Zimri’s death the people of Israel divided into two parts: half followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri. The people that followed Omri prevailed, Tibni died, and Omri reigned (1 Kings 16:21–22). The throne was gained through civil struggle, and the cost of the division left no visible impression on the rule that followed. Omri reigned twelve years over Israel, six of them in Tirzah. He bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, built on it, and named the city after the owner of the hill (1 Kings 16:23–24). Samaria became the seat of the northern kingdom and the symbol of its departure from the Lord.
judgment: Omri wrought evil in the eyes of the Lord and did worse than all that were before him. He walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities (1 Kings 16:25–26). Each king surpassed his predecessor, yet the standard of comparison was always the original departure: the sin of Jeroboam. Omri slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigned in his stead (1 Kings 16:28). His son then exceeded him, as if walking in Jeroboam’s sins were a light thing (1 Kings 16:31). The house Omri built became the house through which Baal worship entered Israel, and the prophet Micah later named the accumulated corruption as the statutes of Omri (Micah 6:16).

verses.text: Then were the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half followed Omri.
But the people that followed Omri prevailed against the people that followed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.
In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign over Israel, twelve years: six years reigned he in Tirzah.
And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill, Samaria.
But Omri wrought evil in the eyes of the Lord, and did worse than all that were before him.
For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he did, and his might that he shewed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So Omri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria: and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.

text.text: And Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord above all that were before him.

And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.

entries.commentary: The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin. Therefore the Most High will make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and those who die in the city the dogs will eat and those in the field the fowls will eat. The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought.

Elah son of Baasha reigns two years, and his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspires against him while he is drunk in a steward's house and kills him. Zimri, on taking the throne, slays all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, according to the word spoken by Jehu against Baasha. All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities. -

Zimri reigns only seven days in Tirzah. When the people encamped against Gibbethon hear he has slain the king, they make Omri, captain of the host, king over Israel. Omri and Israel go up and besiege Tirzah, and when Zimri sees the city taken, he burns the king's house over himself and dies. His death comes for his sins in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and his treason is recorded, treason being punishable by death in that time.

Israel is divided: half follow Tibni son of Ginath and half follow Omri, but Omri's followers prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns. Omri buys the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, builds the city, and names it after Shemer. Omri does worse than all before him, walking in the way of Jeroboam, then sleeps with his fathers, and Ahab his son reigns in his place.

Ahab son of Omri reigns twenty-two years in Samaria and does evil above all that were before him. As if walking in Jeroboam's sins were a light thing, he takes Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians to wife and serves and worships Baal, rearing an altar and a grove, provoking the Most High more than all the kings before him. This mirrors Solomon, who followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and the marrying outside the people that the law forbids because it turns the heart to other gods. In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua. -
